nodes.rationale: Monthly horizon, K=50, VALIDATED (IS +21.0%/yr, OOS +26.5%/yr, OOS Sharpe 0.87) — the opposite-verdict endpoint to E3 in the same factor family.

nodes.label: OPEN universe decision (39 survivors / ~100 large-caps / Trading price_cache)
nodes.rationale: K=20 is only meaningful if the universe supports a real sort: top-20 of 39 is half the universe (tests direction, not magnitude). Recommended (b) ~100 large-caps — a genuine sort without coupling the two projects or inheriting price_cache's verified gaps (next_open 1.1M rows vs 15.7M close, only 3 delistings, median ticker 636 rows).

nodes.label: Diagnostic-not-deployment rule
nodes.rationale: Stated before any data is pulled because it is the easiest rule to break later: picking the best of four cells and deploying it IS in-sample composition — exactly the M10-1 mistake already capped. A winning cell requires a separate prereg on the D1 dual-bar before forward paper enters the conversation, and M12 cannot retroactively rewrite the search-phase terminal claim.

nodes.label: git tag search-phase-closed-v1 (6e8f431)
nodes.rationale: Declared revert point for the whole post-closure phase.

nodes.label: docs/trial_log.json
nodes.rationale: Machine-readable trial extraction; regenerate, never hand-edit. 37 prereg docs on disk, highest recorded attempt 38, 50 declared variants, 1 unresolvable field (E18 verdict) flagged rather than guessed.

nodes.label: scripts/build_trial_log.py
nodes.rationale: Must be re-run before every DSR computation; a stale log silently under-counts as soon as one more variant is tried. Emits null + _unknown for unresolvable fields and nothing downstream may fill them by inference.

nodes.label: Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR)
nodes.rationale: Deflates an observed Sharpe by the number of trials the search actually conducted — the trial count is the single easiest input in the method to fudge, so a DSR run that does not read the trial log has no defensible count.

nodes.label: Declared-variants count is a LOWER BOUND
nodes.rationale: 50 counts only prereg-declared variants; it excludes parameter values explored before pre-registration, the ~90-method survey and dropped-16 list, and abandoned variants never written down. Therefore any DSR computed from 50 is OPTIMISTIC — the direction of error is stated so it cannot be quietly forgotten at the point of use.
nodes.norm_label: declared-variants count is a lower bound

nodes.label: UNRESOLVED 37-vs-38 attempt count
nodes.rationale: Not silently resolved, because picking one to make the arithmetic tidy is exactly what makes a trial count untrustworthy. Rule for DSR: use the LARGER figure — too high is more conservative, too low flatters the strategy; when in doubt the error must point away from significance.

nodes.label: headline_verdict_at_publication is a pointer, not a ruling

nodes.label: Verdict-matcher prefix bug (m10_2 recorded as M10-1's PASS-HR)

nodes.rationale: When a data floor makes the 2000-2013 gate impossible, only one window exists, so no PASS tier may be claimed; the ceiling is PROMISING pending forward confirmation.

nodes.label: M10 Data-Snooping Disclosure
nodes.rationale: M10 designs were composed after seeing 31-32 prior results on the same two windows; mitigations are a published pre-2012 switching mechanism, verbatim-inherited parameters, exactly one new number, and a cap on any in-window pass.

nodes.label: IN-SAMPLE-COMPOSED, Forward Paper Required
nodes.rationale: A numerical pass on a design assembled from known survivors is not a clean pass; it is recorded as in-sample-composed and can only route to forward paper, never a live claim.

nodes.label: No Tuning a FAIL
nodes.rationale: Thresholds and parameters are fixed in the prereg before the run; a failing result is never re-tuned into a pass, and no post-hoc bolt-on de-risking is permitted.

nodes.label: Time-Stop Exit Baseline
nodes.rationale: Adopted as the baseline because C3 found time-stops beat channel exits; any price or trailing stop would have to beat the time-stop-only arm and none is adopted pre-emptively.

nodes.label: Opportunistic vs Routine Insider-Trade Classification
nodes.rationale: A purchase in month m is ROUTINE if the same insider also bought in month m in each of the three prior years, else OPPORTUNISTIC; CMP found only pattern-breaking trades carry information (~82 bps/mo), so E19 trades only the opportunistic subset.

nodes.label: Filing-Date Entry (point-in-time, no lookahead)
nodes.rationale: Entry uses the Form-4 filing date rather than the transaction date because the filing is what is publicly knowable at decision time (filed within 2 business days).

nodes.label: Dividend-Capture Ex-Date Accounting (D/P0 credit)
nodes.rationale: Because prices are dividend-UNADJUSTED, the ex-date drop would read as a pure loss unless the received dividend is credited to P&L; the per-trade return therefore adds a D/P0 term explicitly.

nodes.label: VIX > 20 Regime Switch (STRESS vs CALM)
nodes.rationale: The single new parameter in the M10 arc; 20.0 is the long-run VIX mean / canonical elevated line, sourced from Nagel's published pre-2012 mechanism rather than fit to these windows, with 18/22 reported to bound rather than tune.

nodes.label: C1 FF3-Residual Short-Term Reversal
nodes.rationale: Gate-alive but secondary-dead (19.08% to 2.92% CAGR); its own prereg already declared survivor-universe results uninterpretable.

nodes.label: E6 200-DMA Trend Rotation
nodes.rationale: Secondary-alive but gate-weak (2.66% to 14.47% CAGR) - window-disjoint from C1, which is why fixed-weight blends are arithmetically infeasible for PASS-HR.

nodes.label: E2 Leveraged IBS Mean-Reversion
nodes.rationale: Measured more than half its edge inside the signal-close-to-next-open gap: next-open CAGR 7.98% vs 18.15% close-to-close.

nodes.label: Gap Amortization via 5-Session Hold
nodes.rationale: E2's 1-day hold made the lost first-night gap ~100% of the capture window; a 5-day hold shrinks it to ~20% by holding days 2-5 of the reversion. Load-bearing assumption: if reversion completes on night 1 the extension recovers little.

nodes.label: Causal Pivot Detection (w=5 half-window, confirmed at j+w)
nodes.rationale: A swing high/low at bar j is only usable once w bars of right-side confirmation exist, so decision bar i sees only pivots with j+w <= i. LMW's two-sided kernel smoother is non-causal and is explicitly avoided as look-ahead.

nodes.label: M11 Result: FAIL, Signal-Dead (gate -0.14% CAGR / Sharpe 0.09)

nodes.rationale: Chosen because it is the bridge signal between E3 (failed) and momentum_v2 (validated), not because it is a new idea - holding the signal constant is what makes the constraint factorial interpretable.

nodes.label: 2x2 Factorial: Horizon (10 vs 63 sessions) x Concentration (K=3 vs K=20)
nodes.rationale: Running only the doubly-relaxed cell could not attribute a result to either relaxation; reporting all four cells plus both main effects and the interaction is the entire point.

nodes.label: H_0: Neither Constraint Binds
nodes.rationale: Written down before running precisely so it cannot be quietly discarded if the four cells come out flat.

nodes.label: M12 Verdict Discipline: Diagnostic, Not a Deployment Gate
nodes.rationale: Selecting the best of four cells and deploying it is in-sample composition - the documented M10-1 mistake. A real effect must be re-fixed in a separate prereg and gated on the standard D1 dual-bar before forward paper enters.
nodes.norm_label: m12 verdict discipline: diagnostic, not a deployment gate

nodes.label: Search-Phase Terminal Claim (37 attempts, no cost-surviving OOS edge)
nodes.rationale: Explicitly conditioned on the constraints (K=1-3, days-to-weeks holds, retail costs, free EOD data); M12 extends the map but cannot retroactively un-falsify anything already killed.
nodes.norm_label: search-phase terminal claim (37 attempts, no cost-surviving oos edge)

nodes.label: Existence Spread (low-minus-high DTC), Reported Not Deployable
nodes.rationale: Tests whether the documented sign exists at all in this universe, but is flagged non-deployable because the anomaly's alpha sits in the short (high-DTC) leg and there is no fractional shorting at this capital.
nodes.norm_label: existence spread (low-minus-high dtc), reported not deployable

nodes.label: 10-Session Dissemination-Lag Lookahead Guard
nodes.rationale: Short interest for settlement date S is not disseminated for ~8-9 business days, so entry waits 10 trading sessions past S - a fixed conservative approximation chosen to eliminate lookahead at the cost of signal freshness.

nodes.label: Conditional Volatility Targeting (de-risk only if vol elevated AND trend broken)
nodes.rationale: E18 de-risks on any vol spike including spikes inside an intact uptrend; requiring both conditions keeps the book invested through those, so the interaction must beat E6-alone and E18-alone on gate Sharpe to earn its keep.
nodes.norm_label: conditional volatility targeting (de-risk only if vol elevated and trend broken)

nodes.label: Purged K-Fold with Embargo (K=6, embargo 1%)
nodes.rationale: Labels built from forward windows leak into folds that touch those windows, so standard K-fold reports skill that does not exist; training observations overlapping a test label window are dropped, plus a 1% embargo after each test block.

nodes.label: CPCV (N=6 groups, 2 test groups, 15 combinations)
nodes.rationale: A single train/test split yields one path and one Sharpe - no distribution and no variance across paths; reporting the full distribution is mandatory because with concentrated books median and mean diverge sharply.

nodes.label: Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR)
nodes.rationale: Adjusts an observed Sharpe for trial count, skew/kurtosis, and sample length; a strategy-level test of whether the Sharpe survives the number of trials searched.

nodes.label: Probability of Backtest Overfitting (PBO via CSCV)
nodes.rationale: Selection-level test: the fraction of splits where the in-sample-best configuration underperforms the median OOS. PBO > 0.5 means the selection procedure is worse than random - it measures selection, not edge.
nodes.norm_label: probability of backtest overfitting (pbo via cscv)

nodes.label: Measured Round-Trip Friction Model
nodes.rationale: Friction is the signed gap between the price the simulation assumed and the price actually obtained, computed per fill from live paper fills - never an assumed constant. It ships uncalibrated: n=4 fills cannot estimate a distribution, so it is an instrument, not a number.

nodes.label: Fail-Loud on Missing Measurement (MIN_FILLS_FOR_ESTIMATE = 20)
nodes.rationale: estimate_friction() raises rather than falling back to a constant or a defaulted warning; a caller may proceed only by passing an explicit assumed_bps, which stamps friction_source=ASSUMED on every downstream artifact so no report can present an assumption as a measurement.

nodes.label: Trial Count as Hard Input (larger of the two figures)
nodes.rationale: Read from trial_log.json, raising if missing or older than the newest prereg, because a stale log under-counts trials in exactly the direction that flatters the result; the 37-vs-38 discrepancy is resolved by erring toward more trials, and the count must print in the same block as the DSR.
nodes.norm_label: trial count as hard input (larger of the two figures)

nodes.label: Planted-Edge Falsifier (reported, not gated)
nodes.rationale: A harness that rejects everything is as useless as one that accepts everything, so a synthetic series with a genuinely predictable feature is fed in and must NOT be rejected; otherwise criteria 1-2 are satisfied trivially and the rejections carry no information.

nodes.label: Success Condition: The Harness Must REJECT Things
nodes.rationale: A validation layer that passes noise is not merely weak, it is harmful - it manufactures false confidence in exactly the situation it exists to prevent, so rejection of a worthless signal is pre-registered as the acceptance test before any code is written.
nodes.norm_label: success condition: the harness must reject things

nodes.label: Amended OR-Rule: Rejected if DSR Insignificant OR PBO >= 0.5
nodes.rationale: V1's AND-conjunction was mis-specified: DSR is strategy-level and PBO is selection-level, so requiring both demanded one strategy fail two unrelated tests. A no-edge rule with highly correlated variants has almost no selection to overfit, so its PBO sits near random while DSR correctly says no edge. Both statistics are still reported separately.
nodes.norm_label: amended or-rule: rejected if dsr insignificant or pbo >= 0.5

nodes.label: Amend by Superseding, Never by Rewriting the Original
nodes.rationale: V1 failed its own criterion 2 and that failure stands on the record; amending a criterion by rewriting the document it lives in would erase the evidence that it was ever wrong, which is the entire reason the project pre-registers anything.
nodes.norm_label: amend by superseding, never by rewriting the original

nodes.label: Predicted False Positive: Planted Edge Rejected via PBO 0.514
nodes.rationale: Written down in advance rather than explained away afterwards. Pre-committed handling: report it as a stated limitation of the selection-level axis - PBO is only meaningful when the configuration set represents a genuine selection choice - and do NOT loosen PBO_FAIL_AT or drop the falsifier; a V3 would compute PBO only over real selection sets.
nodes.norm_label: predicted false positive: planted edge rejected via pbo 0.514

nodes.label: Prereg X2b - Short-Side / Long-Short Days-to-Cover, Borrow-Costed
nodes.rationale: Follow-on to X2, which found the short-interest anomaly real but concentrated entirely on the high-DTC short leg and therefore non-deployable long-only; X2b asks the deployability question by costing borrow honestly.

IBS=(close-low)/(high-low) divides by zero there, so signal code must skip a ticker on any high==low day (IBS undefined -> no signal) rather than crash. The other 28 universe tickers were clean.

nodes.label: A raise in a shared helper is inert until you check what CATCHES it
nodes.rationale: 2026-08-13 (record EO, measured): _note_vintage was changed 2026-08-12 to raise on a stale or mixed vintage and proved 5/5 in isolation, yet was swallowed at three reachable sites. Worst was cache_fetch's OWN retry loop - the call sat inside the try guarding prices.fetch, so a vintage verdict printed as '{ticker} attempt N error', slept 20/40/60/80s, refetched 4x and died as 'could not fetch'. run_m12_factorial and run_v1_harness_check caught it per-ticker and continued, so a uniformly stale cache excluded every name in turn: the guard turned 'refuse to run' into 'run on a silently emptied universe', strictly worse than the printing it replaced. Fixed by naming StaleCacheError(RuntimeError), moving the call out of the fetch try, and re-raising in both consumers. Rule: a broad except Exception around a call that can now raise a VERDICT must re-raise that verdict explicitly.
nodes.norm_label: a raise in a shared helper is inert until you check what catches it

nodes.label: scripts/ implicit namespace package -> two StaleCacheError classes
nodes.rationale: 2026-08-13 (record EQ, proven by identity not assumption): scripts/ has no __init__.py and the repo root is on sys.path, so 'import run_e8_squeeze' and 'import scripts.run_e8_squeeze' both succeed and produce TWO DIFFERENT module objects with two different StaleCacheError classes; 'except StaleCacheError' then silently does not match and the guard is swallowed again. Today's consumers are safe (m12 and v1 catch the identical class object, 'is' returns True; zero repo-wide hits for the dotted form). Applies to EVERY cross-script except in scripts/. Rule: import sibling scripts as bare run_x, never scripts.run_x.

nodes.label: D1 Dual-Bar Verdict Protocol
nodes.rationale: Approved by Evan 2026-07-12 (record Appendix AW) as a dated goal AMENDMENT - gate numbers change only by a new dated Evan decision. Adds a pre-registered risk-adjusted tier alongside the unchanged high-return one, because running overlay candidates under the primary bar alone is theater: overlays cannot clear PASS-HR at all. Every prereg fixes ALL THREE labels before running. PASS-RA does not authorize live capital by itself - it only makes a forward-paper candidate.

nodes.label: PASS-HR (High-Return) Gate
nodes.rationale: Net CAGR >= 15% AND maxDD <= 60% in the 2000-2013 gate window, confirmed in 2014->end. The unchanged primary bar. Zero clean passes in the whole program: M10-1 cleared it but is IN-SAMPLE-COMPOSED, and E16 cleared the return leg once at 16.76% CAGR only to breach the DD ceiling at 65.9%.

nodes.label: PASS-RA (Risk-Adjusted) Gate
nodes.rationale: Net Sharpe >= 0.80 in the gate window AND strictly above SPY buy-hold's in BOTH windows AND positive net CAGR in both. Exactly one pass in the program - E18's VIX/VIX3M<1 gate - and it is flagged WEAK because the 2006-13 window has one crash, so the pass largely equals dodging 2008.

nodes.label: Modified-Window PROMISING Cap
nodes.rationale: Short-window data breaks the D1 gate protocol - FINRA SI starts 2021, Reg SHO 2009, crypto ~2015 - so the 2000-2013 hostile-regime gate is unusable there. Rule adopted for M9: each prereg fixes a modified window a priori, discloses the reduced confidence, and CAPS the best achievable verdict at 'PROMISING - needs forward confirmation'. Only full-window experiments can claim D1 tiers.

nodes.label: docs/prereg_TEMPLATE.md
nodes.rationale: The standing template every future prereg copies, folding the research-batch process findings into fixed [STANDING] sections: tiered costs, the decomposition ladder, the time-stop baseline, capped-Kelly sizing, plus D1 dual-bar, asymmetric framing, prereg-before-code hash, tripwire-GREEN done-check, the modified-window cap, and LLM-forward-only.

nodes.label: Pre-Registration-Before-Code Ordering Rule
nodes.rationale: Sacred and provable forever from git log: if backtest-engine code exists before the prereg doc is committed, the project's core claim is dead. When in doubt, commit the doc first. Verified for E1 (prereg 8963e49 at 12:17:29 predates backtest.py 415c527 at 12:24:54, 7m25s later) and E2 (865c09e predates 6ef2b2a the same day). Several later preregs are doc-only commits that predate their runners.

nodes.label: Rung A/B/C Execution-vs-Signal Decomposition Ladder
nodes.rationale: Required in every results doc: Rung A frictionless close-to-close 0 bps, Rung B next-open 0 bps, Rung C next-open plus costs (the graded rung). It separates SIGNAL-DEAD (fails A) from GAP-DWELLER (dies A->B) from COST-GATED (dies B->C), which is what turned a flat 'null' into two named killers.

nodes.label: Time-Stop-Only Baseline Requirement
nodes.rationale: Every strategy reports a time-stop-only exit arm as the honest baseline, and any price-stop variant must BEAT it. C3 justified the rule: its time-stop arm beat the channel exit 6.19% vs 3.62% - the 10-day-low exit was a whipsaw tax, not risk control.

nodes.label: Tiered Cost Model + Liquidity Floor Formalization
nodes.rationale: 1 bp/side broad ETFs, 5 bps/side single stocks and sector ETFs, 15-25 bps or exclude below the floor; liquidity floor formalized as ADV >= $5M AND price >= $5; participation cap declared non-binding at this AUM; a 15 bps/side stress leg reported alongside. The stress leg does real work - it broke M10-1, C1 and X3.
nodes.norm_label: tiered cost model + liquidity floor formalization

nodes.label: Capped Fractional-Kelly Sizing Defaults
nodes.rationale: Capped fractional-Kelly (lambda <= 1/2), fixed-risk r = 1-2%/trade, anti-martingale only, no leverage, with lambda and r frozen per prereg. Engine gotcha behind it: E2 sized on initial capital rather than current NAV and a K=1 3x run sent NAV negative - future engines size on current NAV.

nodes.label: Asymmetric-Falsification Framing
nodes.rationale: On the survivor universe only a FAIL is clean - a PASS is uninterpretable because survivorship flatters exactly the trades the strategy makes. It is why C1's in-window passes were declared UNINTERPRETABLE and why every stock experiment inherits E3's framing. ETF experiments are interpretable in both directions.

nodes.label: LLM Overlays Are Forward-Only (Training-Cutoff Look-Ahead)
nodes.rationale: LLM overlays cannot be backtested honestly, period: any LLM scoring historical dates is partly RECALLING outcomes (Profit Mirage: 50-72% post-cutoff decay; Levy 2026). So the whole LLM shortlist is forward-only treatment arms on the M3 live-paper control, never backtests. Non-negotiable gates when it runs: pinned model ID+version (an upgrade = re-prereg), immutable overlay_log, ticker anonymization, and the tripwire pinned on DETERMINISTIC REPLAY of the log rather than a live model call.

No gate beat the plain 200-DMA on the robust both-windows criterion - but the VIX/VIX3M<1 arm cleared PASS-RA, the program's first tier-pass, flagged WEAK. HY-OAS arm INCONCLUSIVE (FRED free data only ~2023+). An overlay test where PASS-RA is the only reachable tier: without D1 the task would have been pointless.

nodes.label: E19 - Insider Opportunistic-Buy Drift
nodes.rationale: The heaviest ingestion the project attempted (104,496 Form-4s, 39/39 CIKs) and the program's 8th family. FAIL clean and robust: underperforms SPY on CAGR AND Sharpe in BOTH windows. Data was heavily transactionCode-'P' contaminated (BAC alone = 44% of P-buys, including $0.01 1-share artifacts) and the CMP classifier passed 95% through - falsifying the prior prediction that routine filings would absorb it - but a post-hoc de-junk sensitivity cutting entries 6,119->2,675 left the verdict unchanged, so the FAIL is a clean falsification, not a contamination artifact.

nodes.label: E20 - Dividend-Capture Falsification

But the secondary collapses to 2.92% (dead post-2014), 15bps kills it, and survivorship upper-bounds the gate anyway, so the in-window pass is UNINTERPRETABLE. Its residual_series machinery is reused verbatim by the m10_1_nagel live sleeve.

FAIL as predicted (gate 3.62%/Sh 0.37). Key finding: the time-stop-only arm BEATS the channel exit - the 10-day-low exit is a whipsaw tax. Third of three breakout-family kills.

This PERMANENTLY closes the E2 c2c 18.15% mirage: the gap was hiding the DRAWDOWN (2x long into 2000-02/2008 cascades), not alpha. It also sharpens M10-1 - unlevered cross-sectional reversal passes, 2x index MR is an 83%-DD engine, so M10-1's pass is a cross-sectional-SURVIVOR effect, not a general stress-reversion edge.

nodes.rationale: Three isolated Alpaca paper accounts running three pre-registered sleeves since 2026-07-15. Declared the ONLY uncontaminated evidence source the project has (no survivorship, no in-sample composition) and the single open lever after the search phase closed.

nodes.label: M7/M7b catalog experiment arc (E13-E20)
nodes.rationale: Systematic sweep of the documented swing-strategy catalog; every arm FAILed or was data-blocked.

nodes.label: M10 synthesis arc
nodes.rationale: Composed the surviving PROPERTIES of prior experiments into candidate return engines. Binding disclosure: designs made after seeing 31 results on the same two windows carry a severe data-snooping prior, so any in-window pass is capped IN-SAMPLE-COMPOSED.

nodes.label: M10-1 Nagel Switch
nodes.rationale: VIX-gated regime switch (C1 residual reversal when VIX>20, E6 trend when VIX<=20). The program's FIRST numerical PASS-HR in 32 attempts - and labelled PROMISING / FORWARD PAPER REQUIRED, never a clean pass: gate DD clears the 60% ceiling by 0.05pp, fails at a nearby VIX threshold of 18, and inherits C1's survivor-universe uninterpretability.

nodes.label: M10-2 gap-amortized stress IBS
nodes.rationale: FAIL; closes E2's close-to-close mirage permanently by measuring how much of the gap edge is reachable with a multi-day hold.

nodes.label: M11 chart-pattern detector
nodes.rationale: FAIL, signal-dead. Closed the chart-pattern family and showed survivorship bias destroys the apparent pattern edge. Its causal pivot detector was later reused verbatim as a validation-harness subject.

nodes.label: M12 constraint-relaxation factorial
nodes.rationale: 2x2 over horizon and breadth on a frozen 142-name universe. Diagnostic only, no PASS/FAIL issued. Its published SEC numbers were later found wrong (stale-cache contamination) and corrected.

nodes.label: e6_1x live paper sleeve
nodes.rationale: Simplest sleeve, single instrument - chosen to run first precisely because a plumbing bug there is least likely to corrupt the evidence trail.

nodes.label: e18_vixts live paper sleeve
nodes.rationale: Holds its position and returns None with a stated reason whenever VIX or VIX3M is unavailable - it never guesses a signal.

nodes.label: m10_1_nagel live paper sleeve
nodes.rationale: Weekly decision cadence; the sleeve M3 actually exists to validate, since M10-1's pass is in-sample-composed and only forward evidence can make it real.

nodes.label: swing_bot/prices.py price fetcher
nodes.rationale: Built because Trading's price_cache lacks OHLC. Drops any NaN O/H/L/C row, which is what makes an incomplete same-session Yahoo bar fall back safely to the prior complete session.

nodes.label: swing_bot/paper_sleeves.py
nodes.rationale: Sleeve ledger schema plus decide_e6_1x / decide_e18_vixts / decide_m10_1, each reusing the IDENTICAL signal condition as its backtest runner - load-bearing for M3's implementation-fidelity criterion.

nodes.label: swing_bot/alpaca_client.py
nodes.rationale: Ported, not imported, from the Trading repo. Paper base URL default; per-sleeve client factory so the three accounts stay isolated.

nodes.label: swing_bot/costs.py cost model
nodes.rationale: Friction is MEASURED from real fills or it RAISES - no constant fallback. An explicit override taints every downstream artifact with friction_source=ASSUMED so an assumption can never be read as a measurement.

nodes.label: swing_bot/validation.py
nodes.rationale: Houses purged K-fold, CPCV, DSR and PBO; treats the trial log as a hard input that raises if missing or stale.

nodes.label: scripts/daily_swing_paper.py nightly loop
nodes.rationale: One evening run realizes the prior run's pending fill at today's known open, then stores today's close signal as pending for tomorrow - mirroring every backtest runner's signal-at-close/execute-next-open timing.

nodes.label: scripts/daily_swing_paper.bat
nodes.rationale: Pure ASCII by hard rule. Its trailing echo used to swallow the child exit code so the scheduler could only ever report success; now propagates via exit /b %RC%.

nodes.label: scripts/run_e8_squeeze.py (de-facto shared data layer)
nodes.rationale: An experiment runner that became the repo's shared data layer; 31 files import it. That accidental centrality is why every cache defect in it is a project-wide defect.

nodes.label: cache_fetch() shared cache accessor
nodes.rationale: Top god node of the knowledge graph (36 edges, betweenness 0.193, bridging 19 communities). Refetches only on a cache MISS for the tickers the running script names, which is why a partial refresh cannot be assumed to work.

nodes.label: _note_vintage() cache freshness guard
nodes.rationale: Now measures staleness against the CLOCK, not against sibling series: comparing series to each other needs len(distinct)>1, which is unreachable in a single-ticker script, and comparing to the newest date on disk cannot catch uniform staleness because the max equals the value under test.

nodes.label: StaleCacheError exception class
nodes.rationale: A named RuntimeError subclass, so nothing that already caught RuntimeError changes behaviour but a consumer can re-raise it by name ahead of its broad handler.

nodes.label: scripts/prove_cache_guard.py standing proof
nodes.rationale: Eight cases proving the freshness guard actually fires at every swallow site, including a fresh-vintage silence case (a guard that always fires is as useless as one that never does) and a real-network-error case (proving the moved retry loop still retries four times).

nodes.label: scripts/run_m12_factorial.py
nodes.rationale: Truncates the date axis to the EARLIEST final bar and prints MIXED-VINTAGE CACHE loudly, so the contamination that corrupted its own published numbers is now loud instead of silent.

nodes.label: swing_bot.test_frozen frozen tripwire
nodes.rationale: 12 pinned numeric refs at d=+/-0.0000pp plus 17 invariants; the project's required done-check after any change. One invariant scans every scripts/*.py that mentions cache_fetch for an adjustment-convention header.

nodes.label: scripts/build_trial_log.py
nodes.rationale: Extracts DSR's trial count from first-party artifacts (prereg docs, git, results docs, the record) rather than prose, because the trial count is the easiest input in the method to fudge.

nodes.label: docs/trial_log.json machine-readable trial log
nodes.rationale: Records 37 prereg docs, a highest attempt number of 38 and 50 declared variants as a LOWER BOUND. The 37-vs-38 discrepancy was left unresolved on purpose and a pre-registered rule says DSR uses the LARGER figure, since a too-low trial count flatters the strategy.

nodes.label: .e8e9_cache research data layer
nodes.rationale: 292 files in one filename namespace across three shapes; only the 181 bar lists carry a vintage the guard can see. All five vintages are stale, so 'delete the stale entries' has no non-empty complement, and no enumerator or refresh tool exists anywhere in the repo.

nodes.label: Trading repo price_cache (read-only dependency)
nodes.rationale: Split-adjusted, dividend-UNADJUSTED; read-only from this project. Lacks OHLC, which forced this project to build its own fetcher.

nodes.label: Frozen 142-name M12 universe
nodes.rationale: Frozen by a pre-declared cutoff that excluded GS. All 142 still trade today, so the universe is biased in the strategy's favour and only a FAIL is clean.

nodes.label: alpaca_keys.env credential file
nodes.rationale: Gitignore status was verified BEFORE anything else was written to it; confirmed never tracked on any branch by git log --all.

nodes.label: SwingTradingDailyPaper scheduled task
nodes.rationale: Weekly Mon-Fri 19:00 local, one invocation running all three sleeves together. Converted to S4U so it runs unattended without a stored password.

nodes.label: fill_divergence sim-vs-broker instrument
nodes.rationale: Measures real slippage between the simulated and broker fill. Cannot be calibrated yet: n=4 fills against a required 20, three of them the same ticker/side, and the -85.7 bps outlier is a documented discipline break rather than spread.

nodes.label: paper_nav forward-evidence series
nodes.rationale: 20 sessions 2026-07-15..2026-08-12 with exactly one permanent hole at 2026-07-30.

nodes.label: graphify-out/ knowledge graph
nodes.rationale: Rebuilt from 381 nodes / ZERO edges to 725 nodes / 1094 edges. Now a stale oracle: six tracked files still encode 16 invariants and the old timezone rationale and know nothing of the newest code, while a standing rule says to query it first.

nodes.label: Pre-registration before results
nodes.rationale: Every attempt commits a doc-only prereg with fixed rules and criteria, verified that no runner existed at that commit. Rationale: it makes a FAIL uninterpretable-as-tuning and is the one property that keeps a long string of failures evidentially useful. Risk appetite may change gate NUMBERS, never rigor DISCIPLINE.

nodes.label: D1 dual verdict tiers
nodes.rationale: Two pre-declared bars judged together: PASS-HR (high return) and PASS-RA (risk-adjusted). Added so a strategy that is genuinely risk-improving is not scored as a failure by a return-only bar, and vice versa.

nodes.label: PASS-HR gate (CAGR >= 15% and maxDD <= 60%, both windows)
nodes.rationale: Return-centric with a loosened-but-present drawdown ceiling, matching the stated high-return concentrated goal.
nodes.norm_label: pass-hr gate (cagr >= 15% and maxdd <= 60%, both windows)

nodes.label: PASS-RA gate (Sharpe >= 0.80, > SPY both windows, +CAGR both)
nodes.norm_label: pass-ra gate (sharpe >= 0.80, > spy both windows, +cagr both)

nodes.label: Survivorship bias
nodes.rationale: yfinance holds only currently-listed names, so every backtest is upper-bound biased. The standing consequence: on a survivor universe only a FAIL is clean evidence; a PASS is uninterpretable.

nodes.label: Mixed-vintage cache contamination
nodes.rationale: Cache entries are written on whatever day a ticker is first touched, so a universe can hold several end dates. A union date axis then marks short names at ZERO, and because the evaluation window terminates wherever the data stops each series silently sets its own CAGR denominator. It corrupted a committed, pushed results doc.

nodes.label: The 'guard that cannot fire' defect class
nodes.rationale: The project's one recurring defect, headline of five consecutive audits: a threshold below the mathematical minimum of what it guards, a parameter no caller passes, a check needing two series in a single-series script, a raise caught by the function that raises it, and a namespace split that would break an except clause. Standing rule: when you add a guard, prove it fires by feeding it the trigger.
nodes.norm_label: the 'guard that cannot fire' defect class

nodes.label: Swallowed-raise trap
nodes.rationale: A correct raise caught by a broad except in its own caller. Worse than the printing it replaced at the per-ticker sites, where it converted 'refuse to run' into 'run on a silently emptied universe'. Feeding a guard its trigger proves the guard works; it does not prove anyone lets the failure through.

nodes.label: Clock-based staleness measurement
nodes.rationale: Only the clock sits outside the set being tested, so it is the only reference that closes the uniform-staleness case. The checks RAISE rather than print, because printing WAS the defect: the warning scrolls past and the number is believed.

nodes.label: SWING_ALLOW_STALE_CACHE / SWING_MAX_CACHE_STALE_DAYS
nodes.rationale: Escape hatch and tolerance (default 5 calendar days). Deliberately left un-hardened: the allow flag rejects anything but '1' and so fails CLOSED, and a bad tolerance value raises at import - loud, before any broker call - whereas a try/except default would silently discard the operator's stated tolerance.

nodes.label: Append-only record discipline
nodes.rationale: Prior appendices are never edited; a later entry corrects an earlier one and both stand. The one disclosed exception was an entry corrected before it had ever been committed, where both edits made it less flattering.

nodes.label: /landing-check fresh-agent sweep
nodes.rationale: A fresh agent is given the ARTIFACTS only - diff, commits, docs as specimens - and explicitly denied the session's account of what the work did, because a session's recollection is not a source of truth about the repo.

nodes.label: Cold audit method
nodes.rationale: A fresh auditor with no session history and no 'this part is known-good', run precisely because the session that built the code cannot audit it. Repeatedly found that prior fixes were detective but not corrective.

nodes.label: Refute pass over asserted defects
nodes.rationale: Every claimed defect is handed to an independent agent instructed to REFUTE it, defaulting to REFUTED when uncertain. It overturned 8 of 24 claims - mostly dated historical statements that were exact when written and would have been corrupted by 'fixing' them.

nodes.label: One-window death pattern
nodes.rationale: The program's signature failure: a rule works in the stressed window and gives the Sharpe back in the calm one. Confirmed six times across US equity, non-US equity, crypto, credit and gold - which is why trend gating is classified as drawdown control, not return enhancement.

nodes.label: Cost drag as the binding constraint
nodes.rationale: The mechanistic tell is that an effect GROWS when costs triple; turnover falling 50.5x -> 8.3x/yr is what makes the long horizon win. 'The signal is smaller than the toll' is a different and more useful finding than 'the signal does not exist'.
nodes.norm_label: cost drag as the binding constraint

nodes.label: Decorrelation is not the scarce resource, EDGE is
nodes.rationale: Three consecutive decorrelation attempts each cleared a 0.30 correlation bar comfortably (+0.089 / -0.191 / -0.057) and each failed profitability. Uncorrelated return streams are easy to find; ones with a surviving retail-net edge are not.
nodes.norm_label: decorrelation is not the scarce resource, edge is

nodes.label: IN-SAMPLE-COMPOSED verdict cap
nodes.rationale: Any pass from a design built after seeing prior results on the same windows is labelled forward-paper-required and never a live claim, because an in-window pass composed with hindsight is weaker evidence than the falsifications that preceded it.

nodes.label: Signal at close, execute next open
nodes.rationale: Hard rule: EOD data only, no intraday logic until an intraday source exists. The live loop mirrors this exactly so the forward test measures the same rule the backtest did.
nodes.norm_label: signal at close, execute next open

nodes.label: Mandatory liquidity floor
nodes.rationale: Required in any universe filter because at $100-1,000 spread and slippage dominate. For a long stretch it was UNENFORCEABLE - defined once, read nowhere, then read only behind a branch that had never executed.

nodes.label: Split-adjusted / dividend-UNADJUSTED convention
nodes.rationale: Every price consumer must state it in a header comment. Its cost is visible in X8: coupon-bearing TLT is materially understated, so bonds cannot be read cleanly - logged as a data-layer gap, not an experiment limitation.

nodes.label: Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR)
nodes.rationale: Asks whether a Sharpe survives the trial count. Discriminated perfectly three ways: 0.0001 noise / 0.0168 chart patterns / 1.0000 planted edge. At N=50 trials the expected best per-period Sharpe under the null is +0.0694, which is why the rule's annualised 0.695 does not survive deflation.

nodes.label: Probability of Backtest Overfitting (PBO via CSCV)
nodes.rationale: A SELECTION-level test, not a strategy-level one. It is meaningful only over a configuration set that represents a genuine selection choice - asking it about edge was the mis-specification, and it correctly but uselessly rejected a known planted edge at PBO 0.514.
nodes.norm_label: probability of backtest overfitting (pbo via cscv)

nodes.label: Purged K-fold and CPCV
nodes.rationale: K=6 with a 1% embargo; purge+embargo demonstrably removes 70 observations per split (2971 -> 2901), which is the check that it is actually wired in rather than nominally present. CPCV's 15 paths are reported as a distribution because for concentrated books the median is not the mean.

nodes.label: V1 cost model + validation harness
nodes.rationale: Built against a deliberately worthless signal, with an INVERTED done-check: success is the harness REJECTING both subjects. Reported FAIL under its own pre-registered criteria because criterion 2 was mis-specified as an AND of two unrelated tests - not retuned after seeing results.

nodes.label: V2 acceptance-criterion amendment
nodes.rationale: Split the criterion so DSR governs strategy-level rejection and PBO governs selection-level rejection, with either axis able to fire. Written as a NEW dated prereg; V1's failure stands unedited. Its section 4 predicted the resulting false positive before the re-run, and the prediction held.

nodes.label: V3 (scope PBO to genuine selection sets)
nodes.rationale: Deferred until the live loop accumulates enough measured fills - a gate then measured to be UNREACHABLE on the current trajectory.
nodes.norm_label: v3 (scope pbo to genuine selection sets)

nodes.label: Planted-edge falsifier
nodes.rationale: A reported-not-gated control containing a KNOWN edge. It exists because a harness that rejects everything satisfies its acceptance criteria trivially and carries no information.

nodes.label: Search phase closed at 37 attempts
nodes.rationale: A dated decision, not an abandonment: the space defined by free EOD data, days-to-weeks holds, K=1-3, retail costs and $100-1,000 is exhausted, and what remains in the project's own method survey is either 1-12 month horizon or data-gated. Hunting a 38th rule in the same box has low expected value.

nodes.label: HORIZON binds, breadth does not
nodes.rationale: M12's attribution result, and a self-correction: the project had ASSERTED that retail concentration forbade the breadth the premium requires. Tested, breadth lost - K=20 of 142 is a 14% sort that converges toward the equal-weight benchmark, and it actively destroys the horizon gain.

nodes.label: Forward-evidence phase
nodes.rationale: The one open lever after the search closed. It needs elapsed time, not another attempt, and its product is EVIDENCE rather than returns - which is why sleeve correlation matters more here than it would for a return program.

nodes.label: BLOCKED-ON-EVAN discipline
nodes.rationale: Keys, accounts, purchases, credentials and live-ledger writes are reported and never worked around, and a stub is never passed off as live. Applied to Alpaca account creation, the scheduled-task credential, a one-row ledger UPDATE and a paid-data spend ceiling.

nodes.label: S4U logon type for the nightly task
nodes.rationale: Runs unattended without a stored password, replacing an Interactive task that silently lost sessions whenever Evan was logged off while Windows reported zero missed runs.
nodes.norm_label: s4u logon type for the nightly task

nodes.label: Missed-session detector
nodes.rationale: Rewritten as a set difference over the whole series rather than a max(date) comparison, so it can see an INTERIOR hole - which is what 2026-07-30 was.

nodes.label: Batch exit-code swallowing defect
nodes.rationale: In cmd a batch's exit code is its last command's, so a trailing echo made every run report success. Until fixed, every silent failure downstream was structurally invisible to the scheduler.

nodes.label: Implicit namespace-package import hazard
nodes.rationale: scripts/ has no __init__.py and the repo root is on sys.path, so import X and import scripts.X yield two different exception classes and an except clause silently stops matching. Proven safe today by class identity rather than assumption, and binned as a rule for every cross-script except.

nodes.label: Static-blend impossibility proof
nodes.rationale: A red-team result: PASS-HR from any FIXED-weight combination is arithmetically empty because the two windows demand disjoint weights. The only escape is state-conditioning on a causal variable - which is what selected the Nagel Switch.

nodes.label: The overnight-gap assassin
nodes.rationale: The recurring killer identified by the failure decomposition: more than half of a short-horizon edge lives in the close-to-next-open gap that an EOD executor cannot capture.

nodes.label: Pattern Day Trader rule eliminated
nodes.rationale: The $25,000 minimum-equity PDT designation was eliminated effective 2026-06-04 with an 18-month phase-in. Flagged VERIFY-WITH-BROKER rather than fact-on-the-ground, and read as removing an excuse rather than a constraint - the strategies it unlocks are the high-turnover ones the cost arithmetic punishes hardest.

nodes.label: The three live sleeves are ~one strategy
nodes.rationale: m10_1_nagel runs the identical e6 rule on 69.7% of 4,226 sessions; all three are effectively long simultaneously 65.3% of days. Disclosed as an honest CONSEQUENCE of the evidence - nothing uncorrelated and profitable was ever found to deploy - and NOT fixed by editing a running sleeve, which would break its pre-registration and destroy the accumulated forward evidence.
nodes.norm_label: the three live sleeves are ~one strategy

nodes.label: VIX3M source lag inverted the live signal
nodes.rationale: A Yahoo source lag made a stale VIX3M invert e18's live decision; fixed by moving to a CBOE source and clearing stale pending orders.
nodes.norm_label: vix3m source lag inverted the live signal

nodes.label: Intraday-execution guard
nodes.rationale: Added after a re-fire filled a stale SELL inside the session, which would have broken the signal-at-close/execute-next-open contract the whole forward test rests on.

nodes.label: Quantity-aware broker reconcile
nodes.rationale: Closes share drift between the DB ledger and the broker; verified in production when it closed the e18 share fork at a real open.

nodes.label: A session's recollection is not a source of truth
nodes.rationale: Discovered when HEAD was four commits past where the session believed it was; a handoff written from memory would have pointed a fresh session at work already done. The rule: build handoffs from git log, not from what you remember doing.
nodes.norm_label: a session's recollection is not a source of truth

nodes.label: Verify a change against the state it creates
nodes.rationale: The generalized lesson: a fix that corrects a count can invalidate that count by existing. Proving a guard fires in isolation does not prove a caller lets it through, and checking a claim against the state you found does not check it against the state you made.
nodes.norm_label: verify a change against the state it creates

nodes.label: .claude/codebase-memory bins
nodes.rationale: Eleven bins plus an index, required to be updated in the same session as any fact-changing change. The entire research cache data layer had never appeared in any bin - every 'cache' hit referred to the Trading repo's price_cache.

nodes.label: Nagel (RFS 2012) - reversal alpha as liquidity provision
nodes.rationale: Supplied the causal MECHANISM (not a date) that lets a regime switch escape the static-blend impossibility: reversal compensation scales with VIX. Caveat recorded - its 1998-2010 sample overlaps the gate window, so the mechanism is partly in-sample.
nodes.norm_label: nagel (rfs 2012) - reversal alpha as liquidity provision

nodes.label: Gatev, Goetzmann & Rouwenhorst (2006) - pairs distance method
nodes.rationale: Adopted wholesale at its published defaults so the test could not be accused of parameter mining.
nodes.norm_label: gatev, goetzmann & rouwenhorst (2006) - pairs distance method

nodes.label: Do & Faff (2010) - pairs-trading decay
nodes.rationale: Pre-declared as the FAVORED prior so a FAIL could not later be dressed up as a surprise. H0 won, and the decay reproduced independently on this project's own data.

nodes.label: Sullivan, Timmermann & White (1999) - Reality Check on TA rules
nodes.norm_label: sullivan, timmermann & white (1999) - reality check on ta rules

nodes.label: Bajgrowicz & Scaillet (2012) - FDR on DJIA trading rules
nodes.rationale: An investor could never have selected the future best rules ex ante, and in-sample performance is completely offset by low transaction costs.
nodes.norm_label: bajgrowicz & scaillet (2012) - fdr on djia trading rules

nodes.label: Osler (2003) - FX order-book clustering at round numbers
nodes.rationale: The one classical TA concept with a directly observed order-flow mechanism - but wrong asset class and needs intraday data the EOD-only rule forbids.
nodes.norm_label: osler (2003) - fx order-book clustering at round numbers

nodes.label: Barber, Lee, Liu & Odean - Taiwan day-trader tape
nodes.rationale: More than 8 in 10 day traders lose in a typical semiannual period; -23.9 bps/day net.
nodes.norm_label: barber, lee, liu & odean - taiwan day-trader tape

nodes.label: Bessembinder (2018) - skewness of lifetime stock returns
nodes.rationale: 4.3% of stocks account for all net wealth creation, so K=1-3 is a skewness bet whose median draw loses to cash - which is why evaluation must report the DISTRIBUTION, not the mean of a few runs.
nodes.norm_label: bessembinder (2018) - skewness of lifetime stock returns

nodes.label: George & Hwang (2004) - 52-week high
nodes.rationale: The surviving trend evidence is cross-sectional, diversified and 6-12 months; compressing it to K=1-3 over 5-20 days is an extrapolation outside the evidence and must be tested as one.

nodes.label: Hou, Xue & Zhang - concentration and factor premia
nodes.rationale: Supplied the breadth explanation the project asserted for months; M12 tested it and it lost.
nodes.norm_label: hou, xue & zhang - concentration and factor premia

nodes.label: Xia et al. 2026 (arXiv 2605.19337) - audit of 77 LLM-trading studies
nodes.rationale: 2/19 disclose a time-consistent split, 1/19 a transaction-cost model, 0/19 reach full reproducibility.
nodes.norm_label: xia et al. 2026 (arxiv 2605.19337) - audit of 77 llm-trading studies

nodes.label: Zhu et al. 2026 (KTD-Fin) - masked-ticker LLM evaluation
nodes.rationale: With tickers and calendar masked, frontier LLM agents' returns are explained by passive market and style exposure: the alpha is beta.
nodes.norm_label: zhu et al. 2026 (ktd-fin) - masked-ticker llm evaluation

nodes.label: Lo, Mamaysky & Wang (2000) - chart patterns
nodes.rationale: Chart patterns carry incremental distributional information - not a net-of-cost strategy.

nodes.label: Trading repo momentum_v2 (sister project)
nodes.rationale: Top-50 of ~5,200 monthly, validated IS +21.0% / OOS +26.5% / Sharpe 0.87. It is a 1% sort, which is why M12's 14% sort measures sort strength rather than diversification - and why relaxing concentration here would duplicate the sister project rather than inform this one.
